title: Iterators and generators (intro)
learningObjectives: Explain iterators and generators (intro) and use the relevant JavaScript language feature correctly.

understand.concept: An iterator is an object that follows the iterator protocol: it provides a next() method that returns an object containing value and done. An iterable exposes a Symbol.iterator method that returns an iterator. Generator functions, declared with function*, produce iterators and can pause and resume with yield.
understand.whyItMatters: Iterators provide a common way to consume sequences, while generators make custom lazy sequences easier to write. Lazy iteration can avoid building a complete array when values can be produced on demand.
understand.analogy: An iterator is like a person handing over one item at a time and indicating when the list is finished.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript language protocols, primitive identity, and date/time semantics are defined by the language and runtime.

explain.narrative: Each next() call resumes the generator until the next yield. Spreading the generator consumes its remaining values into an array.

examples.explanation: Each next() call resumes the generator until the next yield. Spreading the generator consumes its remaining values into an array.
examples.expectedOutput: Console output demonstrates the behaviour described in the lesson.

practise.guidedTask: Write a generator that yields three lesson labels. Consume it once with next() and once with for...of. Explain why a generator is exhausted after completion.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that uses this feature with normal inputs and edge cases. Explain when this feature is preferable to a simpler alternative.
hints: Read the return value and iteration protocol carefully.
Test duplicate, invalid, and boundary values.
Avoid assuming locale or time-zone output is identical everywhere.

questions.prompt: What does a generator yield to its caller?
options: An iterator result sequence, one value at a time
questions.answer: An iterator result sequence, one value at a time
questions.explanation: A generator pauses at yield and returns iterator results as it is resumed.

questions.prompt: What is a good practice when using advanced JavaScript features?
options: Understand their semantics and test edge cases
Use them everywhere regardless of need
questions.answer: Understand their semantics and test edge cases
questions.explanation: Advanced features are most useful when their specific semantics solve a real problem.
